reason: A is more physically plausible because a nanoscale surface coating could suppress surface-initiated fatigue cracking while leaving the bulk magnetostructural transition—and thus the magnetocaloric effect—largely unchanged, and it provides a direct coated-versus-uncoated falsification test. Its claim of improved bulk tensile strength and its cited evidence are weak, but B is even less grounded: Co can strongly alter MnNiSi-family magnetic and structural transitions, while the asserted grain-boundary segregation, refinement, and ductilization mechanisms have no supporting evidence.
